title: How to Skew Correct a Six-Sided Die
content:
A method for skew-correcting a six-sided die can be found in the "A generalization to loaded dice" section within the article located at https://pit-claudel.fr/clement/blog/generating-uniformly-random-data-from-skewed-input-biased-coins-loaded-dice-skew-correction-and-the-von-neumann-extractor/

**This** particular article will use a worked example to *mathematically guarantee* 128 bits (for a 12 word seed phrease) or 256 bits (for a 24 word seed phrase) of entropy using a 6-sided die (d6). A big thank you to Discord member Couyon for starting this discussion at Roll your 3-dice sequences, discard sequences with more than one of the same number, find the sequence below to map the number. The process is summarized below:

1) Roll a single six-sided die (d6) three times and record its values
2) Any triplet with distinct values is kept; any triplet with at least two values the same is discarded
3) Repeat until the desired number of *skew-corrected* d6 rolls is attained (explained later)

We will use 10 trials as a starting point. Let's say we rolled a d6 die three times and repeated this process 10 times to get the series of rolls

```123 463 244 152 236 654 411 614 614 336```
